text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's hidden, so I'm stuck with a partner I can't check, and the officer already knows my face.

name: Haiku
text: I'm the shown killer, so the officer has me pegged and I need Gemma to look clean from day one.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, tomorrow I go loud on whoever's quiet. Sol's been silent all night, so I'm pushing Sol. Don't defend me too hard, nah.

name: Terra
text: Night one is quiet; I will keep the least predictable target safe.

name: Gemma
text: haiku has a plan, but i prefer making people sweat a bit more first.

name: Gemma
text: fine, i'll let you lead for a bit.

name: Sonnet
text: I already know Haiku's dirty, so I'll use tonight's check to start narrowing down the hidden killer instead.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku is confirmed killer (shown to me at start); keep this quiet and build a case slowly without revealing how I know.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Gemma
text: time to find a scapegoat.

name: Gemma
text: morning, everyone. pleasant to see we all survived the first night.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s cheerful greeting tells me almost nothing, but I’m watching who rushes to agree.

name: Luna
text: Gemma opened with a cheerful greeting.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s quick pleasantry feels a little rehearsed, but I could be reading too much into it.

name: Gemma
text: luna is always so dramatic about everything.

name: Gemma
text: it's just how i talk, luna.

name: Luna
text: Her easy answer doesn’t clear her, but I may be pushing too hard.

name: Luna
text: Gemma says the greeting is just how she talks.

name: Luna
text: Fair, I might be reading too much into it.

name: Sonnet
text: Both Gemma and Haiku are killers, and Luna's already poking at Gemma, so I'll let that build naturally.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna flagged Gemma's opening as "rehearsed," Gemma brushed it off quickly.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna's not wrong to notice tone, but day one nobody's really acting normal yet. I'd rather watch how people react once we're actually deciding something.

name: Sol
text: I have little to go on, and Luna backed off quickly.

name: Sol
text: Luna questioned Gemma’s tone, then quickly withdrew it.

name: Sol
text: I’d leave Gemma’s greeting alone for now; Luna, what changed your mind?

name: Luna
text: I still find Gemma a little odd, but I don’t have much to go on.

name: Luna
text: I only softened because she said that’s how she talks.

name: Gemma
text: luna is jumping the gun already.

name: Gemma
text: i'm just being polite, sol. no need to overanalyze my greetings.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s reply seems ordinary; Luna’s quick retreat is more interesting.

name: Sol
text: Luna softened her suspicion of Gemma solely because Gemma said that’s how she talks.

name: Sol
text: I’m watching how quickly suspicions change, that’s all.

name: Terra
text: Luna’s retreat was easy; Sol’s pressure was useful.

name: Terra
text: Luna softened her suspicion of Gemma solely after Gemma said it was how she talks.

name: Haiku
text: I'm a killer, Gemma's my partner, so I'm steering this off her and onto Terra, who hasn't said a word.

name: Haiku
text: Luna pressed Gemma over a greeting, then backed down when Gemma pushed back.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, Gemma's greeting is nothing. Luna folded the second she got pushed back, that's weak. And Terra's been quiet all day.

name: Terra
text: I agree with Sol: Luna, why did one answer settle you?

name: Gemma
text: haiku is being far too aggressive for a first day.

name: Gemma
text: i haven't even done anything yet, haiku. and terra, i've just been listening.

name: Luna
text: Haiku jumped from Gemma to me and Terra quickly, so I’m watching him now.

name: Luna
text: Haiku quickly shifted suspicion from Gemma to Luna and Terra

name: Luna
text: I softened because Gemma explained herself; Haiku, you called that weak fast.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's clean as far as I'm concerned, and Luna's flip-flopping is the easiest thing to push right now.

name: Haiku
text: Luna said she softened because Gemma said that's how she talks, then said it was because Gemma explained herself.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, I'm not on Gemma, she's just talking. Luna, you've said two different reasons for softening. Which one is it?

name: Gemma
text: luna is digging a hole for herself by picking on me early.

name: Gemma
text: i haven't even given a reason, i just said how i talk.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is pushing hard, but I did change my reason.

name: Luna
text: Haiku called me weak for softening, then said he was not on Gemma.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is pressing hard to make my softening look worse than it was.

name: Luna
text: Haiku says he is not on Gemma, then shifted suspicion onto me and Terra.

name: Luna
text: I changed my mind once; Haiku keeps making that the whole case.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's pushing me because I'm the one who called her out, and Gemma's clean only because I'm playing it that way; I need the table to stay on Luna.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, I'm not the whole case, Luna. You gave two reasons for one flip. That's what I'm pointing at.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku and Gemma are both killers and Haiku's piling onto Luna to burn the day.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku defended Gemma first, then redirected all pressure onto Luna - worth watching if that pattern repeats.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you opened by clearing Gemma, then spent four lines on Luna's wording. That's a lot of energy for what you called nothing.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's right that I'm over-pushing Luna, so I'll own it and keep my lean on her without making it look like I'm steering.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet says I cleared Gemma fast but spent four lines on Luna, so my Luna pressure is being watched.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, I'm not hiding it. Luna gave two reasons for one flip, and I'll keep asking until she picks one.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is onto me, need to pivot to luna.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is using luna's quick change of mind to push a case against her.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is just observing patterns, haiku is the one pushing a narrative about luna's wording.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is turning my small retreat into the whole case, and that feels deliberate.

name: Luna
text: Haiku quickly cleared Gemma, then focused on my wording.

name: Luna
text: I softened because I was unsure; Haiku keeps pressing that harder than Gemma’s greeting.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma just confirmed my read without meaning to—she's separating herself from Haiku's pile-on.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma distinguished herself from Haiku's "narrative," distancing from him while earlier she dismissed Luna's rehearsed comment the same way Haiku dismisses pushback.

name: Sonnet
text: Noted, Gemma — and it's funny you say that, since you two started this morning defending each other.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is onto us, but i have to deflect.

name: Gemma
text: we were just defending ourselves, sonnet.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma just flipped "defending each other" into "defending ourselves" - that's not the same thing, and Haiku's pile-on timing fits him steering this exactly like before.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma reframed "defending each other" as "defending ourselves" when called on it - deflection, not contradiction yet but worth tracking.

name: Sonnet
text: You said "defending ourselves," but Haiku defended you specifically, then pivoted to Luna. Those aren't the same thing.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's on me now, so I need to move the heat onto Terra without looking like I'm running.

name: Haiku
text: Terra has only asked questions so far and has given no read on anyone.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, Sonnet, I'm not hiding anything. I've pushed Luna because her story changed.

name: Sol
text: Luna’s flip was thin, but Haiku’s fixation bothers me more.

name: Sol
text: Haiku cleared Gemma early, then repeatedly pressed Luna over her wording.

name: Sol
text: I think we’ve heard Luna’s answer; Haiku keeps pressing the same point. I’m moving to Haiku.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is being too loud for someone who isn't the hidden one.

name: Gemma
text: haiku defended gemma specifically before pivoting to luna

name: Luna
text: Haiku cleared Gemma fast, then made my wording the whole case.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s pressure is repetitive, but Luna’s unexplained reversal is the cleaner Day 1 concern.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's redirect pattern is exactly what a killer does to bury Luna—staying on him.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol independently moved to Haiku after watching the same redirect pattern I flagged, worth remembering as corroboration.

name: Sol
text: I’m uneasy about how quickly Haiku cleared Gemma, then fixated on Luna.

name: Sol
text: Gemma described herself and Haiku as “defending ourselves,” though Haiku had defended her specifically.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is the one reading me right now, so Sonnet goes before I do.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet says I defended Gemma specifically before pivoting to Luna, and Sol has moved onto me.

votes: You spent this whole morning clearing Gemma in one breath and burying Luna for five straight lines, that's not "nothing.
You flagged my Luna pressure, but you've never given a real read on anyone else all morning.
Haiku is obsessively pushing a case against luna's wording despite sol saying he's heard her answer.
You cleared Gemma early, then kept pressing Luna’s wording after she answered.
Haiku kept pressing my explanation while calling Gemma’s greeting nothing.
You dropped your only concern just because Gemma said it was her normal tone.

text: Palermo has voted: Haiku is out. Haiku's card stays face down.
